categories.name: Tourism & Heritage

categories.description: Follow annual international visitor and receipts indicators, then explore India’s UNESCO World Heritage properties by inscription year. subgroups.name: International Visitor Trends
subgroups.title: 🧳 International Visitor Trends

subgroups.name: World Heritage Sites

subgroups.name: Global Tourism Comparison

indicators.title: Real GDP growth
indicators.subtitle: Annual real GDP growth
indicators.details:
Annual percentage growth in real gross domestic product. This is a historical national-accounts series, not a forecast.

Sourced from the World Bank indicator NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG.

indicators.title: CPI inflation
indicators.subtitle: Consumer prices
indicators.details:
Consumer price inflation tracks the annual change in the cost of a representative basket of goods and services. It is a broad measure of household purchasing-power pressure.

The series is useful alongside growth, exchange-rate, and trade indicators because imported costs and domestic demand can move inflation in different directions. Values are annual and come through the World Bank open API.

indicators.title: Per capita Net National Income
indicators.subtitle: Per capita NNI at current prices in Indian Rupees
indicators.details:
Per capita Net National Income (NNI) measures national income divided by population in current Indian Rupees. It expanded from ₹63,462 in FY2012 to ₹2.18 Lakh in FY2026.

Sourced from MOSPI National Accounts Statistics and official Economic Survey statements.

series.source: MOSPI National Accounts Statistics & Economic Survey (Per Capita Net National Income - NNI at Current Prices in INR)

indicators.title: Per capita GNI in PPP dollars
indicators.subtitle: GNI per capita in Purchasing Power Parity current international $
indicators.details:
GNI per capita converted to international dollars using purchasing power parity (PPP) rates, accounting for domestic price differences.

Sourced from World Bank Open Data indicator NY.GNP.PCAP.PP.CD.

datasets.label: Per capita GNI in PPP dollars

series.source: World Bank Open Data NY.GNP.PCAP.PP.CD (GNI per capita, PPP in current international $)

indicators.title: GST collections
indicators.subtitle: Gross monthly GST revenue
indicators.details:
GST collections are a high-frequency signal of recorded consumption and production moving through India's indirect-tax system. Strong receipts can reflect higher activity, improved compliance, price effects, or a combination of these factors.

The monthly series is collated from the Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 9.1. It should not be confused with a forecast or an estimate.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Fiscal deficit
indicators.subtitle: Union fiscal deficit as share of GDP
indicators.details:
The fiscal deficit is the gap between government expenditure and receipts excluding borrowings. It indicates how much the public sector needs to finance during a fiscal year.

The annual series is collated from official Economic Survey table 2.4 Excel files across previous editions and reported as a share of GDP.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 2.4; fiscal deficit as percent of GDP

indicators.title: IIP growth
indicators.subtitle: Industrial production
indicators.details:
Industrial production measures activity across mining, manufacturing, and electricity. It is a useful complement to GDP because it responds more directly to changes in factory output and infrastructure-linked production.

The monthly General IIP index is collated from Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 9.2; MOSPI remains the authoritative Indian source.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Rupee exchange rate
indicators.subtitle: INR per US dollar
indicators.details:
This series expresses the Indian rupee required to purchase one US dollar. A rising value means rupee depreciation against the dollar, all else equal.

Monthly exchange-rate observations are collated from Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 9.4, with RBI DBIE linked as the official portal.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Trade share of GDP
indicators.subtitle: Exports plus imports as share of GDP
indicators.details:
Trade openness compares the combined value of exports and imports with GDP. It gives context for how strongly India's output is connected to external demand, imported inputs, and global price movements.

This is a ratio rather than a rupee total, so it can rise because trade grows or because GDP changes. The series is sourced through the World Bank open API.

indicators.title: Foreign exchange reserves
indicators.subtitle: Total reserves including gold
indicators.details:
Foreign-exchange reserves are external assets held by the monetary authority, including gold in this indicator. They help provide resilience against external-payment stress and exchange-rate volatility.

Reserve adequacy should be read with imports, debt, and the current account rather than treated as a standalone score. The displayed series is annual and denominated in current US dollars.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Bank credit
indicators.subtitle: Domestic credit to private sector
indicators.details:
Domestic credit to the private sector measures financial-sector lending relative to the size of the economy. It can signal whether businesses and households have expanding or tightening access to finance.

Credit growth is not automatically positive: the composition, repayment quality, and cost of borrowing matter. This annual ratio is a structural indicator, not a substitute for RBI monthly banking statistics.

indicators.title: Eight-core industries
indicators.subtitle: Core industrial production index
indicators.details:
The eight-core industries index tracks major infrastructure-linked sectors including coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement, and electricity.

It is an important industrial activity companion to IIP and is collated from Economic Survey table 9.2.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Indian crude oil basket
indicators.subtitle: Average crude oil price
indicators.details:
The Indian crude oil basket price tracks an indicative average of crude prices relevant to India's import exposure. It helps explain fuel-cost pressure, inflation risk, and the external trade bill.

This is a crude price indicator, not a retail petrol or diesel price index. It is collated from Economic Survey table 9.3.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Fuel consumption
indicators.subtitle: Petroleum product consumption
indicators.details:
Fuel consumption measures petroleum product demand and is a useful activity proxy for transport, industry, and household energy use.

It is not a fuel price index. The dashboard labels it explicitly as consumption and sources it from Economic Survey table 9.4.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Merchandise exports
indicators.subtitle: Goods exports
indicators.details:
Merchandise exports measure the value of goods sold abroad. They connect the dashboard to external demand, foreign exchange earnings, and manufacturing competitiveness.

The monthly values are collated from Economic Survey table 9.4 and should be interpreted with imports and the current account.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Merchandise imports
indicators.subtitle: Goods imports
indicators.details:
Merchandise imports measure the value of goods purchased from abroad. They capture domestic demand, imported inputs, energy exposure, and pressure on the trade balance.

The monthly values are collated from Economic Survey table 9.4 and are not the same as total services-inclusive imports.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Merchandise trade balance
indicators.subtitle: Goods exports minus goods imports
indicators.details:
The monthly merchandise trade balance is calculated as goods exports minus goods imports. Positive values indicate a surplus and negative values a deficit.

This national total excludes services and does not identify balances with individual countries or regions.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 9.4; calculated as merchandise exports minus merchandise imports (national balance, not partner-specific)

indicators.title: Merchandise balance by trading partner
indicators.subtitle: Exports minus imports for leading partners
indicators.details:
This chart compares India's reported merchandise exports and imports with its leading trading partners for the latest year with matching observations. Positive values indicate a surplus; negative values indicate a deficit.

UN Comtrade reports exports on an FOB basis and imports on a CIF basis, so values are not perfectly symmetric. The chart covers goods only, not services, and is limited to the leading partners with verified code mappings.

series.source: UN Comtrade API, India merchandise trade by partner (2025); exports FOB minus imports CIF, top partners by trade value

indicators.title: GDP per capita
indicators.subtitle: Current US dollars per person
indicators.details:
GDP per capita divides the value of economic output by population. It is a broad scale indicator for comparing the economy over time, but it does not describe inequality, household income, or quality of life by itself.

The current-dollar series is sensitive to exchange rates and inflation. Read it alongside real growth and purchasing-power measures for a more complete picture.

indicators.title: Current account balance
indicators.subtitle: Balance as share of GDP
indicators.details:
The current account records trade in goods and services, income flows, and transfers with the rest of the world. A deficit means the country is spending more foreign exchange on these flows than it receives during the period.

This indicator connects directly to reserves, the rupee, and external financing conditions. It is shown as a share of GDP to make changes in national scale easier to compare.

indicators.title: Broad money
indicators.subtitle: Money supply as share of GDP
indicators.details:
Broad money captures currency and deposits available across the financial system. Relative to GDP, it provides a long-run view of liquidity and financial deepening.

It is not a direct measure of inflation or spending. Credit conditions, velocity, policy rates, and the distribution of deposits all influence how money supply affects the economy.

indicators.title: Tax revenue
indicators.subtitle: Tax revenue as share of GDP
indicators.details:
Tax revenue shows how much public revenue is collected through taxes relative to the size of the economy. It helps put fiscal capacity and public-service financing in a longer-run context.

The ratio can change because collections move, GDP moves, or both. It does not identify tax burden distribution or distinguish every type of levy.

indicators.title: Government consumption
indicators.subtitle: General government final consumption
indicators.details:
Government final consumption measures public-sector spending on goods and services relative to GDP. It is a useful context signal for the size of direct government demand in the economy.

This is not the same as the fiscal deficit: transfers, capital spending, receipts, and borrowing are treated differently in national accounts.

indicators.title: Foreign direct investment
indicators.subtitle: Net FDI inflows as share of GDP
indicators.details:
Foreign direct investment captures net cross-border investment intended to establish a lasting interest in an enterprise. Relative to GDP, it shows how important foreign investment flows are compared with national output.

A single year can be volatile because of large transactions, restructurings, or exceptional deals. It should be read with the current account and reserves.

indicators.title: Domestic savings
indicators.subtitle: Gross domestic savings as share of GDP
indicators.details:
Gross domestic savings is the portion of national output not used for final consumption. It provides a macro view of the resources potentially available for domestic investment.

The indicator does not show which households, firms, or public institutions save, nor whether savings are invested productively. Its value is strongest when compared with investment and external financing.

indicators.title: Indian Matrix publication cadence
indicators.subtitle: Articles published per week
indicators.details:
This graph tracks the public publication cadence of Indian Matrix articles. It adds the Substack source as a transparent, updateable public-data signal rather than treating article frequency as an economic or crime statistic.

The weekly RSS snapshot is collected by the pipeline and linked to Indian Matrix with appreciation for its visual public-data work.

indicators.title: Indian market indices
indicators.subtitle: Sensex, Nifty, and Nifty VIX; rebased to 100
indicators.details:
This combined graph compares India's major equity-market indices and volatility using one normalized base-100 view. It makes direction and relative movement readable despite the different scales of the Sensex, Nifty, and VIX.

The monthly observations are collated from Economic Survey table 9.3. This is a market-context dashboard, not investment advice, and rebasing means the plotted values are relative rather than index levels.

series.source: BSE and NSE index histories, rebased to 100

indicators.title: Global equity market comparison
indicators.subtitle: BSE Sensex vs S&P 500, FTSE 100, Nikkei 225, and Shanghai Composite; rebased to 100
indicators.details:
This graph compares India's primary equity benchmark (BSE Sensex) against leading global market indices (S&P 500, FTSE 100, Nikkei 225, Shanghai Composite) rebased to 100.

It illustrates the long-run compounding and relative performance of Indian capital markets alongside the world's major financial hubs.

series.source: BSE India, S&P Dow Jones, FTSE Russell, Nikkei Inc., SSE; Base 100 = 2000

indicators.title: World top economies GDP comparison
indicators.subtitle: GDP trajectories of India, US, China, Germany, Japan, and UK
indicators.details:
This chart plots the gross domestic product of India alongside the world's largest economies (United States, China, Germany, Japan, and United Kingdom) in current US dollars.

It contextualizes India's rise from an emerging developing economy following independence to one of the world's top 5 economic powerhouses.

series.source: World Bank API NY.GDP.MKTP.CD (GDP in current USD Trillion)

indicators.title: India sectoral market engines
indicators.subtitle: Nifty IT, Nifty Bank, Nifty Auto, Nifty Energy, and Sensex; rebased to 100
indicators.details:
This series tracks key sectoral engines of India's stock market expansion—Technology, Banking & Financials, Automotive, and Energy—rebased to 100 alongside the benchmark Sensex.

It reveals how different industry pillars have spearheaded growth across economic cycles.

indicators.title: Global inflation benchmark comparison
indicators.subtitle: Consumer price inflation in India, US, and Euro Area
indicators.details:
This indicator compares consumer price inflation rate trends across India, the United States, and the Euro Area.

Reading India's inflation alongside major global central bank economies highlights how global commodity shocks, monetary policy, and exchange rates impact domestic price stability.

series.source: World Bank API FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG (Annual CPI inflation %)

indicators.title: Union Budget total expenditure
indicators.subtitle: Union budget total spending trajectory
indicators.details:

Sourced from official Union Budget Expenditure statements.

series.source: Union Budget Documents, Ministry of Finance (Total Central Expenditure in INR Lakh Crores)

indicators.title: Union Budget YoY growth
indicators.subtitle: Annual percentage increase in Union expenditure
indicators.details:
Year-on-year percentage increase in central budget allocation.

Reflects fiscal policy expansion across economic cycles.

series.source: Union Budget of India, Ministry of Finance (Annual Central Expenditure YoY Growth %)

indicators.title: Union capital expenditure (Capex)
indicators.subtitle: Central budget capital expenditure for asset creation
indicators.details:
Capital Expenditure (Capex) allocation for roads, railways, ports, defense, and infrastructure creation.

Highlights India's strategic pivot toward asset building and long-term capital formation.

series.source: Ministry of Finance Budget Statements (Central Government Capital Outlay / Capex in INR Lakh Crores)

indicators.title: Gross tax revenue YoY growth
indicators.subtitle: Annual percentage growth in gross central tax collections

series.source: Controller General of Accounts (CGA) & Union Budget (Gross Central Tax Revenue Annual YoY Growth %)

indicators.title: Automobile domestic sales

indicators.details:
Annual domestic sales of passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, three-wheelers, and two-wheelers as reported by SIAM. The headline series is total domestic sales, with category trends shown as separate chart lines.

SIAM's public table currently covers FY2008-09 through FY2013-14 only. This chart does not extrapolate the data or substitute production/registrations for sales.

indicators.title: Real household consumption per capita
indicators.subtitle: Household final consumption per person, constant 2015 US dollars
indicators.details:
Households and non-profit institutions serving households (NPISHs) final consumption expenditure per capita, expressed in constant 2015 US dollars. It provides a long-run, inflation-adjusted signal of material consumption per person.

It is an average, not a measure of distribution or each household's purchasing power, and it does not capture unpaid work or public services. Sourced from World Bank indicator NE.CON.PRVT.PC.KD.

indicators.title: WPI inflation
indicators.subtitle: Wholesale price inflation
indicators.details:
Wholesale price inflation tracks price movement at the producer and bulk-trade level. It can reveal input-cost pressure before those changes fully appear in consumer prices.

WPI is not included in the Economic Survey monthly HFI tables used by this pipeline. The Office of the Economic Adviser remains the official source, but its public portal does not currently expose a stable automated export for this dashboard.

series.source: Office of Economic Adviser WPI monthly workbook

indicators.title: Power consumption
indicators.subtitle: Electricity demand
indicators.details:
Power consumption is a high-frequency activity signal that reflects demand from households, services, and industry. It can move with weather, economic activity, and electrification.

The monthly series is collated from Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 9.1. It measures electricity use, not generation capacity or reliability.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: E-way bills
indicators.subtitle: Goods movement compliance volume
indicators.details:
E-way bills track electronically documented movement of goods. They provide a useful logistics and formal-commerce signal that complements GST collections.

The series is a transaction volume, not a rupee value or direct GDP estimate. It is collated from Economic Survey table 9.1.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Rail freight traffic
indicators.subtitle: Domestic rail freight
indicators.details:
Rail freight traffic reflects movement of bulk commodities and industrial inputs through the rail network. It provides a physical-economy signal alongside digital and tax indicators.

The series is reported in thousand tonnes and comes from Economic Survey table 9.1.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Port cargo traffic
indicators.subtitle: Cargo handled at ports
indicators.details:
Port cargo traffic captures goods handled through India's ports and gives context for external trade and domestic supply chains.

It is a volume measure and should be read with merchandise exports, imports, and trade share rather than used as a price indicator.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Iron ore production
indicators.subtitle: National iron ore mining output
indicators.details:
Iron ore is the primary raw material for steelmaking and industrial infrastructure. India is among the world's largest iron ore producers, led by Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and Karnataka.

Data is sourced from the Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM) and Ministry of Mines.

series.source: Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM) & Ministry of Mines (Iron Ore Production Output in Million Tonnes)

indicators.title: Bauxite production
indicators.subtitle: Bauxite ore mining output
indicators.details:
Bauxite is the principal ore for aluminium smelting, vital for aerospace, power transmission, automotive, and packaging industries.

Sourced from IBM and Ministry of Mines annual mineral reports.

series.source: IBM & Aluminium Association of India (Bauxite Production Output in Million Tonnes)

indicators.title: Refined copper production
indicators.subtitle: Refined copper metal production
indicators.details:
Refined copper is essential for electrical grids, electric vehicles, electronics, and urban infrastructure.

Data collated from Ministry of Mines and Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL).

series.source: Ministry of Mines & Hindustan Copper (Refined Copper Production Output in Thousand Tonnes)

indicators.title: Manganese ore output
indicators.subtitle: Manganese ore mining production
indicators.details:
Manganese ore is a crucial alloy element in steel manufacturing and battery technologies.

Sourced from Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM) Annual Mineral Statistics.

series.source: Indian Bureau of Mines Annual Mineral Statistics (Manganese Ore Production Output in Lakh Tonnes)

indicators.title: Coal production trajectory
indicators.subtitle: Domestic coal mining output
indicators.details:
Coal is India's primary baseload energy source, fueling thermal power stations, steel plants, and heavy manufacturing.

Sourced from Coal Controller's Organisation and Ministry of Coal.

series.source: Coal Controller's Organisation & Ministry of Coal (Total Domestic Coal Production in Million Tonnes)

indicators.title: Lignite production
indicators.subtitle: Lignite mining output
indicators.details:

Sourced from NLC India Limited and Ministry of Coal.

series.source: NLC India & Ministry of Coal (Lignite Production Output in Million Tonnes)

indicators.subtitle: Domestic crude petroleum output
indicators.details:
Domestic crude oil production from onshore and offshore fields (Mumbai High, Assam, Rajasthan, KG Basin) supplies domestic refineries alongside energy imports.

indicators.title: Natural gas production

indicators.title: UPI activity
indicators.subtitle: UPI transaction volume
indicators.details:
UPI transaction volume shows the scale of digital payments processed through India's real-time payments infrastructure. It is a useful activity and digitisation signal, especially when paired with transaction value.

The monthly volume series is collated from Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 9.2; NPCI remains the authoritative product-statistics source.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: UPI transaction value
indicators.subtitle: Annual UPI transaction value trajectory
indicators.details:
Annual transaction value processed via Unified Payments Interface (UPI). It highlights the massive scale of real-time digital payments in India's retail economy.

Sourced from National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) and RBI.

series.source: NPCI & Reserve Bank of India (UPI Annual Transaction Value in INR Lakh Crores)

indicators.title: Credit card spends
indicators.subtitle: Annual credit card POS & e-commerce spends
indicators.details:
Total annual spending by consumers using credit cards at point-of-sale (POS) terminals and e-commerce portals.

Sourced from Reserve Bank of India Payment System Indicators.

series.source: Reserve Bank of India Payment System Indicators (Annual Credit Card Transaction Spends in INR Lakh Crores)

indicators.title: Debit card POS spends
indicators.subtitle: Annual debit card POS transaction spends
indicators.details:
Annual consumer expenditure processed via debit cards at merchant POS terminals, excluding cash ATM withdrawals.

Sourced from Reserve Bank of India Payment System Statistics.

series.source: Reserve Bank of India Payment System Data (Annual Debit Card POS Transaction Spends in INR Lakh Crores)

indicators.title: Active credit cards
indicators.subtitle: Credit cards in circulation
indicators.details:
Total active credit cards issued by banks in India, showing expanding formal consumer credit access.

Sourced from Reserve Bank of India.

series.source: Reserve Bank of India Payment System Statistics (Active Credit Cards in Circulation in Crore Cards)

indicators.title: Active debit cards
indicators.subtitle: Debit cards in circulation
indicators.details:
Total active debit cards issued by financial institutions, driven by PM Jan Dhan Yojana bank account expansion.

Sourced from Reserve Bank of India.

series.source: Reserve Bank of India Payment System Statistics (Active Debit Cards in Circulation in Crore Cards)

indicators.title: RBI Digital Payments Index
indicators.subtitle: RBI DPI index trajectory
indicators.details:
Comprehensive index built by Reserve Bank of India to measure payment enablement, infrastructure, performance, and consumer centricity (Base 100 = March 2018).

Sourced from Reserve Bank of India.

series.source: Reserve Bank of India DPI Index (RBI Digital Payments Index; Base 100 = March 2018)

indicators.title: Infant Mortality Rate (IMR)
indicators.subtitle: Infant deaths per 1,000 live births
indicators.details:
Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) measures deaths of infants under one year per 1,000 live births. India achieved a steep reduction from 88.6 in 1990 down to 23.0.

Sourced from Sample Registration System (SRS) Bulletins & World Bank.

series.source: Sample Registration System (SRS), Registrar General of India & World Bank SP.DYN.IMRT.IN (Infant Mortality Rate per 1,000 live births)

indicators.title: Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR)
indicators.subtitle: Maternal deaths per 100,000 live births
indicators.details:
Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) measures maternal deaths per 100,000 live births. India dropped below the SDG target milestone down to 89 per 100k.

Sourced from SRS Special Bulletins on Maternal Mortality & WHO/UNICEF.

series.source: SRS Special Bulletin on Maternal Mortality in India & WHO/UNICEF (Maternal Mortality Ratio per 100,000 live births)

indicators.title: Population
indicators.subtitle: Total population
indicators.details:
Population provides the denominator and demographic context for many other indicators. A growing population can expand the workforce and consumer base while also increasing demand for jobs, housing, health, and infrastructure.

This is a count of people, not a welfare measure. Per-capita indicators and age structure are needed to understand how demographic change affects living standards.

indicators.title: Unemployment rate
indicators.subtitle: Share of the labour force without work
indicators.details:
The unemployment rate measures the share of the labour force that is without work but available for and seeking employment. It does not capture underemployment or people who have stopped looking for work.

Labour-market comparisons require care because survey design and informal employment affect measurement. This annual series is a useful macro context signal rather than a complete employment dashboard.

indicators.title: Electricity access
indicators.subtitle: Population with access to electricity
indicators.details:
Electricity access measures the share of the population with access to electricity. It is a core infrastructure and living-conditions indicator with direct relevance to households, schools, businesses, and digital services.

Coverage does not fully describe reliability, affordability, or quality of supply. The series is annual and sourced through the open World Bank API.

indicators.title: Internet users
indicators.subtitle: Individuals using the internet
indicators.details:
Internet use measures the share of people using the internet. It provides a broad signal of digital access and the potential reach of online services, payments, education, and commerce.

The metric does not measure connection speed, affordability, quality, or intensity of use. Those dimensions require more detailed telecom and household datasets.

indicators.title: Life expectancy
indicators.subtitle: Life expectancy at birth
indicators.details:
Life expectancy at birth estimates the average years a newborn would live under current mortality conditions. It is a high-level outcome indicator for population health and social development.

It is not an individual prediction and does not reveal regional, gender, or income differences. Trends should be interpreted alongside health-system and demographic data.

indicators.title: Defence expenditure
indicators.subtitle: Military expenditure as share of GDP
indicators.details:
Military expenditure tracks defence spending relative to the size of the national economy. It measures military resource allocation across peacetime and security challenges.

Data comes through the World Bank open API and SIPRI military expenditure database.

indicators.title: India defence exports
indicators.subtitle: Annual defence exports from India
indicators.details:
India's defence exports have expanded significantly as part of indigenous manufacturing and Make in India defence initiatives.

Data is collated from official Ministry of Defence Department of Defence Production (DDP) statistics.

series.source: Ministry of Defence, Department of Defence Production (DDP); India Defence Exports in INR Crores

indicators.title: Value of defence production
indicators.subtitle: Total value of indigenous defence production
indicators.details:
Total value of defence production captures manufacturing output across Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs), ordnance factories, and private sector defence enterprises.

Official data is published by the Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence.

series.source: Ministry of Defence (DDP) annual report statistics; Value of Indigenous Defence Production in INR Crores

indicators.title: Defence stockpile index
indicators.subtitle: SIPRI arms inventory & capability index
indicators.details:
SIPRI Trend Indicator Value (TIV) measures the volume of conventional military capability and major weapons stockpiles transferred and maintained.

It provides a long-run comparative measure of military equipment inventory.

series.source: Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) Arms Transfers Database & Stockpile TIV Index

indicators.title: Defence production & exports engine
indicators.subtitle: Defence production vs exports trajectory
indicators.details:
This combined graph compares total indigenous defence production alongside defence export growth in INR Crores.

It illustrates the structural transition of India's defence industrial base toward export competitiveness.

series.source: Ministry of Defence (DDP) open statistics; Total Defence Production vs Defence Exports in INR Crores

indicators.title: Defence allocation
indicators.subtitle: Share of total Union budget expenditure
indicators.details:
Defence allocation tracks military budget spending as a percentage of overall Central Government Expenditure.

Data is collated from official Ministry of Finance Union Budget allocation documents.

series.source: Union Budget of India Documents & Ministry of Finance Budget Allocation Data (% of Total Central Expenditure)

indicators.title: Defence R&D expenditure
indicators.subtitle: DRDO & defense research spending
indicators.details:
Defence R&D expenditure measures capital and revenue allocation for indigenous weapons development, missile technology, and military research.

Data is sourced from DRDO and Ministry of Defence annual standing committee reports.

series.source: DRDO Annual Reports & Ministry of Defence R&D Expenditure (INR Crores)

indicators.title: Defence modernization capital outlay
indicators.subtitle: Capital acquisition spending for armed forces
indicators.details:
Capital acquisition outlay reflects funds allocated for procuring weapons, aircraft, naval frigates, artillery, and modern military hardware.

Official statistics are published by the Ministry of Defence.

series.source: Ministry of Defence Capital Outlay Statements & Parliamentary Standing Committee Reports (INR Crores)

indicators.title: India arms imports trend
indicators.subtitle: SIPRI arms import Trend Indicator Value (TIV)
indicators.details: SIPRI arms imports index tracks conventional weapon import volumes. The declining trend highlights India's structural shift from foreign import dependency toward indigenous manufacturing.

series.source: SIPRI Arms Transfers Database (Trend Indicator Value - TIV)

indicators.subtitle: Intentional homicides per 100,000 people
indicators.details:
The intentional homicide rate is a broad violence indicator measuring deaths caused by another person per 100,000 population. It is useful as a long-run public-safety context signal, but it does not cover every violent incident.

The World Bank series provides modern historical coverage and should be interpreted alongside NCRB crime data, whose definitions and reporting systems vary by year.

indicators.title: Maoist / LWE annual fatalities
indicators.subtitle: Annual deaths in LWE violence
indicators.details:
Annual fatalities in Left-Wing Extremist violence across affected states, collated from official MHA annual reports and SATP compiled records.

It shows the structural decline in LWE violence over 22 years as security coverage and developmental interventions expanded across affected districts.

series.note: Annual total fatalities (civilians, security personnel, and perpetrators) in Left-Wing Extremist violence across affected states.
series.source: Ministry of Home Affairs LWE Division Annual Reports & SATP Fatalities Database

indicators.title: Terrorist attacks
indicators.subtitle: India attacks in GTD-derived open data
indicators.details:
The Global Terrorism Database is a reputable open research dataset covering terrorist events internationally from 1970 onward. This dashboard uses the India rows published by Our World in Data, with GTD provenance.

It is not an official Government of India dataset, and its event definitions differ from MHA and NCRB reporting. The series is not presented as a complete 1947-present history.

series.source: Our World in Data; Global Terrorism Database-derived series

indicators.title: Terrorism fatalities
indicators.subtitle: Deaths in India GTD-derived attacks
indicators.details:
This graph counts fatalities associated with India rows in the GTD-derived public series. It complements the attack-count graph by showing human cost rather than event frequency.

It is not an official Government of India dataset and does not provide a complete 1947-present history.

series.source: Our World in Data; Global Terrorism Database-derived fatalities

indicators.title: Terrorist attacks per million people
indicators.subtitle: GTD-derived attacks normalized by population
indicators.details:
Annual India attack counts divided by the World Bank population series and expressed per million residents. This supports population-scaled comparisons over time; it is a derived measure, not a separate official count.

Coverage is limited to years shared by the GTD-derived attack series and World Bank population data.

series.source: Derived from Our World in Data GTD-derived India attack/fatality series and World Bank population series; coverage is limited to shared years

indicators.title: Terrorism fatalities per million people
indicators.subtitle: GTD-derived deaths normalized by population
indicators.details:
Annual fatalities associated with GTD-derived India attacks divided by the World Bank population series and expressed per million residents. This is a derived rate, not an official government terrorism count.

Coverage is limited to years shared by the GTD-derived fatalities series and World Bank population data.

series.source: Derived from Our World in Data GTD-derived India attack/fatality series and World Bank population series; coverage is limited to shared years

indicators.title: Fatalities per terrorist attack
indicators.subtitle: GTD-derived annual deaths divided by annual attacks
indicators.details: Annual India terrorism fatalities divided by annual GTD-derived attack counts. It describes aggregate lethality by year and is not an estimate of the probability that an individual attack causes fatalities. Years with zero attacks are left blank.

series.source: Derived from Our World in Data GTD-derived India attack/fatality series and World Bank population series; coverage is limited to shared years

indicators.title: NCRB crime indicators
indicators.subtitle: Crime in India 2023 rates by category
indicators.details:
The National Crime Records Bureau publishes Crime in India tables covering reported offences, crime rates, and related public-safety measures. Editions are not consistently comparable across years, so this card shows a single-year (2023) snapshot across crime categories rather than a fabricated multi-year trend.

Values are official Crime in India 2023 rates per 100,000 population (per 100,000 children for crimes against children), compiled and cited on Wikipedia from NCRB Crime in India 2023 Volumes I-III.

series.note: NCRB Crime in India 2023 rates per 100,000 population by category (per 100,000 children for crimes against children), compiled from official Crime in India 2023 Volumes I-III. A single-year snapshot, not a multi-year trend, because NCRB editions are not consistently comparable across years.

indicators.title: Overall violent incidents
indicators.subtitle: Comparable all-India incident series
indicators.details:
No single official open series currently combines violent crime, Maoist violence, and terrorism consistently across India.

This card stays visible as a research target so the dashboard does not add incompatible NCRB, MHA, and GTD definitions into a misleading total.

series.note: Total reported IPC cognizable violent crime cases across India (murder, attempt to murder, rape, kidnapping, dacoity, robbery, rioting).

indicators.title: LWE civilian casualties
indicators.subtitle: Civilians killed in Maoist insurgency violence
indicators.details:
MHA describes civilian and security-force casualties in LWE violence, but the current public page does not expose a stable annual category table.

This series is sourced from the South Asia Terrorism Portal (SATP), a secondary, non-official source that compiles a year-wise civilian/security-force/perpetrator breakdown from news reports for its Maoist Insurgency tracker. It uses a different classification and count than MHA's own 2004-2025 aggregate of 8,956 deaths, so the two figures should not be summed or treated as the same series.

series.note: South Asia Terrorism Portal (secondary, non-official source) 'Maoist Insurgency' fatality breakdown, not MHA's own category data. MHA's public page only publishes the 2004-2025 aggregate (8,956 deaths) without this breakdown.

indicators.title: LWE security-force casualties
indicators.subtitle: Security forces killed in Maoist insurgency violence
indicators.details:
MHA identifies security-force casualties as a distinct LWE impact category, but no stable annual machine-readable series is currently published on the public page.

This series is sourced from the South Asia Terrorism Portal (SATP), a secondary, non-official source with its own Maoist Insurgency classification and news-based provisional counts. It is not the same series as MHA's own 2004-2025 aggregate of 8,956 deaths.

series.note: South Asia Terrorism Portal (secondary, non-official source) 'Maoist Insurgency' fatality breakdown, not MHA's own category data. MHA's public page only publishes the 2004-2025 aggregate (8,956 deaths) without this breakdown.

indicators.title: LWE perpetrator casualties
indicators.subtitle: Maoist/LWE cadre killed in insurgency violence
indicators.details:
The public MHA material does not provide a comparable annual perpetrator-casualty series.

This series is sourced from the South Asia Terrorism Portal (SATP), a secondary, non-official source reporting Maoist/CPI(Maoist) cadre killed under its own Maoist Insurgency classification, distinct from MHA's official aggregate.

series.note: South Asia Terrorism Portal (secondary, non-official source) 'Maoist Insurgency' fatality breakdown, not MHA's own category data. MHA's public page only publishes the 2004-2025 aggregate (8,956 deaths) without this breakdown.

indicators.title: NCRB IPC crime rate
indicators.subtitle: Total cognizable IPC crime rate per 100k
indicators.details:
The IPC cognizable crime rate tracks total reported Indian Penal Code offences per 100,000 population across 7 decades of post-independence Crime in India reports.

Note that changes in reporting, police registration, and population censuses affect long-term comparability.

series.note: Total reported cognizable IPC crime rate per 100,000 population across official Crime in India annual reports.
series.source: NCRB Crime in India historical volumes & Ministry of Home Affairs reports

indicators.title: Crimes against women rate
indicators.subtitle: Reported crimes per 100k female population
indicators.details:
This indicator tracks reported offences against women per 100,000 female population, including cruelty by husband/relatives, assault, kidnapping, and sexual offences.

Increased reporting can reflect greater public awareness and filing under revised legal definitions as well as baseline changes.

series.note: Crime rate against women per 100,000 female population in India.
series.source: NCRB Crime in India annual reports (Crimes against Women section)

indicators.title: Cyber crime case volume
indicators.subtitle: Registered cyber crime cases in India
indicators.details:
Cyber crime cases track registered offences under the Information Technology Act and cyber-enabled IPC crimes.

The rapid increase reflects nationwide digital adoption, online financial services, and expanded cyber police reporting.

series.note: Annual registered cyber crime cases across India.
series.source: NCRB Cyber Crime statistics (IT Act & IPC cyber offences)

indicators.title: Economic offences rate
indicators.subtitle: Cheating, fraud & forgery per 100k
indicators.details:
Economic offences measure financial crimes including criminal breach of trust, forgery, cheating, and counterfeiting per 100,000 population.

Data is sourced from official NCRB Crime in India annual volumes.

series.note: Economic offences (forgery, cheating, fraud, breach of trust) rate per 100,000 population.
series.source: NCRB Crime in India Economic Offences chapters

indicators.title: Indian live election results
indicators.subtitle: Candidate vote totals in currently published Lok Sabha and State Assembly by-elections
indicators.details: Top 30 candidates by currently reported vote totals from the Election Commission of India results portal. The chart is refreshed every three hours when the portal publishes data; the linked dataset preserves all parsed constituency and candidate rows. ECI displayed results are provisional until Form 20 is published. Historical Lok Sabha and Assembly result archives are not included because a stable, openly accessible official archive was not verified.

indicators.title: 2018 Presidential Candidate Total Receipts
indicators.subtitle: President candidate campaign-finance totals by party
indicators.details:
Federal Election Commission candidate-summary totals for the 2018 filing cycle. Total Receipts are aggregated by candidate party. Presidential candidate totals use party as the grouping because the FEC summary file does not report state presidential vote totals. The 2018, 2022 and 2026 filing cycles are midterm years, not Presidential election years.

These are campaign-finance amounts, not votes, turnout, or public contributions alone. Candidate summaries include authorized committees and may be revised when amended reports are processed.

series.note: 2018 FEC candidate-summary totals for President candidates. Total receipts are summed by candidate party. These are campaign-finance aggregates, not votes, turnout, or public contributions alone. FEC summaries may be revised as amended reports are processed.
